75: Increases the target ship's heat as a percentage of its maximum heat capacity by this amount per shot. Only half as effective when the target's shields are up.
76: Reduces the target ship's energy as a percentage of its energy capacity by this amount per shot. Only half as effective when the target's shields are up.
77: Energy consumed per shot. A weapon will not fire if the ship's batteries do not have at least this amount of energy stored.
80: Hull damage dealt to your ship per shot.
81: Shield damage dealt to your ship per shot.
82: Reduces the ship's energy. Ionization slowly wears off over time.
83: Increases the chance of weapon failure for some time after this weapon is fired.
84: Reduces the ship's turn rate, acceleration, and top speed. Slowing wears off over time.
85: Allows weapon damage to "leak through" to the ship's hull even if shields are up. Shield disruption wears off over time, but imparting disruption on yourself does not lose effectiveness as your shields become more leaky.
86: Shield damage dealt to your ship over time by this weapon per shot.
87: Hull damage dealt to your ship over time by this weapon per shot.
88: Fuel damage dealt to your ship over time per shot.
89: Heat damage dealt to your ship over time per shot.
90: Energy consumed per shot, as a percentage of the ship's total energy capacity.
91: Heat generated per shot, as a percentage of the ship's maximum heat capacity.
92: Fuel used or lost per shot, as a percentage of the ship's total fuel.
93: Hull damage dealt to your ship per shot, as a percentage of your total hull strength.
94: Shield damage dealt to your ship per shot, as a percentage of your total shield strength.
95: Maximum inaccuracy of this weapon, in degrees. A value of one means the weapon's aim will be at most one degree off-target.
96: Everything within this distance (including friendly ships) will be damaged when the weapon hits something.
97: This projectile's resistance to anti-missile shots.
98: The power of the anti-missile shots. Higher values make it easier to destroy stronger projectiles.
99: The velocity that this weapon pulls flotsam toward itself.
100: A measure of how well this weapon prevents damage to valuable materials while mining. Weapons with a positive precision result in higher yields, while a negative precision results in lower yields. Some minable objects are tougher than others, and are therefore less susceptible to having their yields altered.
101: This ship needs crew to operate, but has no bunks.
102: This ship's outfits are producing so much heat that it will overheat the moment it takes off. You must either add more cooling or remove some of the outfits that are producing heat.
103: This ship does not have any source of energy to power its systems. You must install some sort of generator.
104: This ship does not have enough fuel to provide energy to power its systems. You must increase the fuel capacity.
105: This ship is unable to move. You must install thrusters.
106: This ship is unable to turn. You must install steering systems.
107: This ship does not have enough bunks for its crew. It could become unresponsive at random times.
108: This ship is too cold to use some of its engines while idle. Its movement may be hindered if it does not have another way of generating heat.
109: This ship's only thruster is an afterburner. It may be unable to move if the afterburner runs out of fuel.
110: This ship has a reverse thruster but no forward thruster. It could be very difficult to maneuver.
